bibl.title: An open science resource for establishing reliability and reproducibility in functional connectomics

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A TEST-RETEST RESOURCE BUILT SO THAT RELIABILITY ITSELF CAN BE MEASURED - 40 repeat-scan datasets from 36 laboratories at 18 institutions, published as the instrument for checking every other instrument in functional connectomics
span.quote: It is our hope that among its many possible uses, the CoRR repository will facilitate the: (1) Establishment of test-retest reliability and reproducibility for commonly used MR-based connectome metrics, (2) Determination of the range of variation in the reliability and reproducibility of these metrics across imaging sites and retest study designs, (3) Creation of a standard/benchmark test-retest dataset for the evaluation of novel metrics.

span.label: how reliable and reproducible the many rfMRI-derived connectome measures actually are, and what data would be needed to find out
span.quote: Unfortunately, the field lacks a data platform by which researchers can rigorously explore the reliability of the many indices that continue to emerge. Such a platform is crucial for the refinement and evaluation of novel methods, as well as those that have gained widespread usage without sufficient consideration of reliability.

span.label: the CoRR repository, its standardised metadata, a quality-assurance battery run over every dataset, and a minimal set of derivatives computed identically across sites
span.quote: It is our hope that among its many possible uses, the CoRR repository will facilitate the: (1) Establishment of test-retest reliability and reproducibility for commonly used MR-based connectome metrics, (2) Determination of the range of variation in the reliability and reproducibility of these metrics across imaging sites and retest study designs, (3) Creation of a standard/benchmark test-retest dataset for the evaluation of novel metrics.

span.label: method
span.quote: It is our hope that among its many possible uses, the CoRR repository will facilitate the: (1) Establishment of test-retest reliability and reproducibility for commonly used MR-based connectome metrics, (2) Determination of the range of variation in the reliability and reproducibility of these metrics across imaging sites and retest study designs, (3) Creation of a standard/benchmark test-retest dataset for the evaluation of novel metrics.

span.label: reliability treated as a measurable property of a measure rather than an assumption about it
span.quote: Unfortunately, the field lacks a data platform by which researchers can rigorously explore the reliability of the many indices that continue to emerge. Such a platform is crucial for the refinement and evaluation of novel methods, as well as those that have gained widespread usage without sufficient consideration of reliability.

span.label: aggregation of previously collected test-retest imaging datasets, de-identified, released without quality screening, with a published quality-metric battery and derivative computation for comparison across sites
span.term: aggregation of previously collected test-retest imaging datasets, de-identified, released without quality screening, with a published quality-metric battery and derivative computation for comparison across sites
span.quote: Consistent with the established FCP/INDI policy, all data contributed to CoRR was made available to users regardless of data quality. Justifications for this decision include the lack of consensus within the functional imaging community on criteria for quality assurance, and the utility of ‘lower quality’ datasets for facilitating the development of artifact correction techniques.

span.label: THE MEASURES WERE IN WIDE USE BEFORE ANYONE COULD CHECK THEM: `THE FIELD LACKS A DATA PLATFORM by which researchers can rigorously explore the reliability of the many indices that continue to emerge. Such a platform is crucial for the refinement and evaluation of novel methods, AS WELL AS THOSE THAT HAVE GAINED WIDESPREAD USAGE WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CONSIDERATION OF RELIABILITY.` The resource is the instrument for checking the instruments
span.quote: Unfortunately, the field lacks a data platform by which researchers can rigorously explore the reliability of the many indices that continue to emerge. Such a platform is crucial for the refinement and evaluation of novel methods, as well as those that have gained widespread usage without sufficient consideration of reliability.

span.label: AND WHERE A DEFINITION DOES NOT EXIST THE PAPER SAYS SO AND GIVES THE CONVENTION INSTEAD: `THERE IS NO EXACT DEFINITION OF THE MINIMUM TIME for detecting developmental effects across scans, THOUGH DESIGNS TYPICALLY SPAN AT LEAST 3-6 MONTHS`. A boundary that everyone uses and nobody has fixed
span.quote: Scan repeated at a distant time-point not believed to be developmentally equivalent. There is no exact definition of the minimum time for detecting developmental effects across scans, though designs typically span at least 3–6 months

span.label: AND WHERE THE COMMUNITY HAS NO CRITERIA, THE POLICY IS TO PUBLISH EVERYTHING: `all data contributed to CoRR was MADE AVAILABLE TO USERS REGARDLESS OF DATA QUALITY. Justifications for this decision include THE LACK OF CONSENSUS WITHIN THE FUNCTIONAL IMAGING COMMUNITY ON CRITERIA FOR QUALITY ASSURANCE, and the UTILITY OF `LOWER QUALITY` DATASETS for facilitating the development of artifact correction techniques.` The exact opposite policy to a published exclusion list, taken for the same reason - there is no agreed criterion
span.quote: Consistent with the established FCP/INDI policy, all data contributed to CoRR was made available to users regardless of data quality. Justifications for this decision include the lack of consensus within the functional imaging community on criteria for quality assurance, and the utility of ‘lower quality’ datasets for facilitating the development of artifact correction techniques.

span.label: and the release carries a disclaimer about what it does NOT mean: `THE ABSENCE OF SCREENING FOR DATA QUALITY IN THE DATA RELEASE DOES NOT MEAN THAT THE INCLUSION OF POOR QUALITY DATASETS IN IMAGING ANALYSES IS ROUTINE PRACTICE for the contributing sites.` An empty state stated as a claim rather than left to be inferred
span.quote: However, the absence of screening for data quality in the data release does not mean that the inclusion of poor quality datasets in imaging analyses is routine practice for the contributing sites.

span.label: AND THE ARTEFACT IS ITSELF RELIABLE, WHICH IS WORSE THAN NOISE: `MOTION ITSELF HAS MODERATE TEST-RETEST RELIABILITY, and appears to CONTRIBUTE TO RELIABILITY WHEN LOW, though it COMPROMISES RELIABILITY WHEN HIGH`. A subject who moves the same way twice makes the measurement look reproducible - the confound and the signal have the same statistical signature
span.quote: Specifically, Yan and colleagues found that motion itself has moderate test-retest reliability, and appears to contribute to reliability when low, though it compromises reliability when high

span.label: AND AN ACQUISITION PARAMETER MOVES A DERIVED MEASURE, WITH THE MECHANISM NAMED: `In the case of fALFF, site-specific differences CAN BE DIRECTLY RELATED TO THE TEMPORAL SAMPLING RATE (that is, TR), as LOWER TR DATASETS INCLUDE A BROADER RANGE OF FREQUENCIES IN THE DENOMINATOR - thereby REDUCING THE RESULTING fALFF SCORES ... rfMRI estimates CAN BE HIGHLY SENSITIVE TO ACQUISITION PARAMETERS`
span.quote: In the case of fALFF, site-specific differences can be directly related to the temporal sampling rate (that is, TR; see Figure 3 ), as lower TR datasets include a broader range of frequencies in the denominator—thereby reducing the resulting fALFF scores (differences in aliasing are likely to be present as well). This note of caution about fALFF raises the general issue that rfMRI estimates can be highly sensitive to acquisition parameters

span.label: THE SITE IS A SIGNAL: `for all the derivatives, THE MEAN VALUE OR COEFFICIENT OF VARIATION OBTAINED FOR A SITE WAS HIGHLY RELIABLE`. Whatever else the measures capture, they reliably capture WHERE THE SCAN WAS TAKEN
span.quote: As can be seen in Supplementary Figure 4 , for all the derivatives, the mean value or coefficient of variation obtained for a site was highly reliable.

span.label: and the authors REFUSED TO NORMALISE THAT AWAY, on purpose: `We OPTED TO NOT USE increasingly popular standardization approaches ... in the calculation of derivative values, as the test-retest framework PROVIDES USERS A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO CONSIDER THE RELIABILITY OF SITE-RELATED DIFFERENCES.` The variation is left visible because it is the subject
span.quote: We opted to not use increasingly popular standardization approaches (for example, mean-regression, mean centering +/− variance normalization) in the calculation of derivative values, as the test-retest framework provides users a unique opportunity to consider the reliability of site-related differences.

span.label: AND THE PAPER DOES NOT DO THE ANALYSIS ITS TITLE PROMISES, AND SAYS SO: `While FORMAL TEST-RETEST RELIABILITY OR REPRODUCIBILITY ANALYSES ARE BEYOND THE SCOPE OF THE PRESENT DATA DESCRIPTION, we illustrate the broad range of potential questions that can be answered`. It is a resource for establishing reliability, not an establishment of it
span.quote: While formal test-retest reliability or reproducibility analyses are beyond the scope of the present data description, we illustrate the broad range of potential questions that can be answered for rfMRI, dMRI and sMRI using the resource.

span.label: and the open questions are printed as questions rather than as gaps to be inferred: `HOW RELIABLE ARE IMAGE QUALITY METRICS? ... Can reliability and reproducibility be used to optimize imaging analyses? HOW CAN SUCH OPTIMIZATIONS AVOID BEING DRIVEN BY ARTIFACTS SUCH AS MOTION? ... WHICH FEATURES BEST DIFFERENTIATE ONE INDIVIDUAL FROM ANOTHER?`
span.quote: Additional questions may include: How reliable are image quality metrics? How does reliability and reproducibility impact prediction accuracy? How do imaging modalities (for example, rfMRI, dMRI, sMRI) differ with respect to reproducibility and reliability? And within modality, are some derivatives more reliable than others? Can reliability and reproducibility be used to optimize imaging analyses? How can such optimizations avoid being driven by artifacts such as motion? How much information regarding inter-individual variation is shared and distinct among imaging metrics? Which features best differentiate one individual from another?

span.label: AND THE POOR-QUALITY DATA ARE KEPT BECAUSE THEY ARE THE POINT: `the inclusion of datasets with significant artifacts related to factors such as motion are PARTICULARLY VALUABLE, as it enables THE DETERMINATION OF THE IMPACT OF SUCH REAL-WORLD CONFOUNDS on reliability and reproducibility`
span.quote: For CoRR, the inclusion of datasets with significant artifacts related to factors such as motion are particularly valuable, as it enables the determination of the impact of such real-world confounds on reliability and reproducibility

span.label: a published quality-metric battery - SNR, FBER, EFC, smoothness, ghost-to-signal, framewise displacement, DVARS, global correlation - computed identically over every contributed dataset
span.note: eliminates: site differences being attributed to biology when they are properties of the scanner, and it bound: `the battery of quality metrics revealed NOTABLE VARIATIONS IN IMAGE PROPERTIES ACROSS SITES` · outcome: held
span.quote: Mean framewise displacement (FD) 29 . A measure of subject head motion, which compares the motion between the current and previous volumes. This is calculated by summing the absolute value of displacement changes in the x, y and z directions and rotational changes about those three axes. The rotational changes are given distance values based on the changes across the surface of a 50 mm radius sphere.

span.label: screening poor-quality datasets out of the release
span.note: eliminates: nothing, and deliberately so: `MADE AVAILABLE TO USERS REGARDLESS OF DATA QUALITY` because of `THE LACK OF CONSENSUS ... ON CRITERIA FOR QUALITY ASSURANCE` and because the artefacts are what artefact-correction research needs · outcome: absent-declared-unreported
span.quote: Consistent with the established FCP/INDI policy, all data contributed to CoRR was made available to users regardless of data quality. Justifications for this decision include the lack of consensus within the functional imaging community on criteria for quality assurance, and the utility of ‘lower quality’ datasets for facilitating the development of artifact correction techniques.

span.label: standardisation of derivative values across sites (mean-regression, mean centering, variance normalisation)
span.note: eliminates: nothing here, refused on purpose: `We OPTED TO NOT USE increasingly popular standardization approaches ... as the test-retest framework provides users a unique opportunity to CONSIDER THE RELIABILITY OF SITE-RELATED DIFFERENCES` · outcome: absent-declared-unreported
span.quote: We opted to not use increasingly popular standardization approaches (for example, mean-regression, mean centering +/− variance normalization) in the calculation of derivative values, as the test-retest framework provides users a unique opportunity to consider the reliability of site-related differences.

span.label: a formal test-retest reliability analysis of the derivatives
span.note: eliminates: nothing in this paper - stated as out of scope: `formal test-retest reliability or reproducibility analyses ARE BEYOND THE SCOPE OF THE PRESENT DATA DESCRIPTION` · outcome: absent-declared-unreported
span.quote: While formal test-retest reliability or reproducibility analyses are beyond the scope of the present data description, we illustrate the broad range of potential questions that can be answered for rfMRI, dMRI and sMRI using the resource.

span.label: subject head motion
span.quote: Mean framewise displacement (FD) 29 . A measure of subject head motion, which compares the motion between the current and previous volumes. This is calculated by summing the absolute value of displacement changes in the x, y and z directions and rotational changes about those three axes. The rotational changes are given distance values based on the changes across the surface of a 50 mm radius sphere.

span.label: Regional Homogeneity
span.quote: Regional Homogeneity (ReHo) 38–40 . The synchronicity of a voxel’s time series and that of its nearest neighbors based on Kendall’s coefficient of concordance to measure the local brain functional homogeneity.

span.label: data quality
span.quote: Consistent with the established FCP/INDI policy, all data contributed to CoRR was made available to users regardless of data quality. Justifications for this decision include the lack of consensus within the functional imaging community on criteria for quality assurance, and the utility of ‘lower quality’ datasets for facilitating the development of artifact correction techniques.

span.label: `developmentally equivalent` - UNDEFINED BY THE FIELD AND FILLED BY CONVENTION: `THERE IS NO EXACT DEFINITION OF THE MINIMUM TIME for detecting developmental effects across scans, though designs TYPICALLY SPAN AT LEAST 3-6 MONTHS`
span.quote: Scan repeated at a distant time-point not believed to be developmentally equivalent. There is no exact definition of the minimum time for detecting developmental effects across scans, though designs typically span at least 3–6 months

span.label: `data quality` - HAS NO AGREED CRITERION IN THIS FIELD, which is the stated reason nothing is screened out: `THE LACK OF CONSENSUS WITHIN THE FUNCTIONAL IMAGING COMMUNITY ON CRITERIA FOR QUALITY ASSURANCE`
span.quote: Consistent with the established FCP/INDI policy, all data contributed to CoRR was made available to users regardless of data quality. Justifications for this decision include the lack of consensus within the functional imaging community on criteria for quality assurance, and the utility of ‘lower quality’ datasets for facilitating the development of artifact correction techniques.

span.label: `Regional Homogeneity (ReHo)` - `the SYNCHRONICITY of a voxel's time series and that of its NEAREST NEIGHBORS based on KENDALL'S COEFFICIENT OF CONCORDANCE`. A neighbourhood, a statistic, and a name
span.quote: Regional Homogeneity (ReHo) 38–40 . The synchronicity of a voxel’s time series and that of its nearest neighbors based on Kendall’s coefficient of concordance to measure the local brain functional homogeneity.

span.label: `intrinsic functional connectivity` - operationalised down to a coordinate and a diameter: `the mean time series from a SPHERICAL REGION OF INTEREST (DIAMETER=8 MM) CENTERED IN PCC` and `Pearson's correlation ... Fisher r-to-z transformed`
span.quote: Intrinsic Functional Connectivity (iFC) of Posterior Cingulate Cortex (PCC) 41 . Using the mean time series from a spherical region of interest (diameter=8 mm) centered in PCC (x=−8, y=−56, z=26) 42 , functional connectivity with PCC is calculated for each voxel in the brain using Pearson’s correlation (results are Fisher r-to-z transformed).

span.label: `head motion` - operationalised as framewise displacement, itself defined by a geometric convention: rotations are converted to distances `BASED ON THE CHANGES ACROSS THE SURFACE OF A 50 MM RADIUS SPHERE`
span.quote: Mean framewise displacement (FD) 29 . A measure of subject head motion, which compares the motion between the current and previous volumes. This is calculated by summing the absolute value of displacement changes in the x, y and z directions and rotational changes about those three axes. The rotational changes are given distance values based on the changes across the surface of a 50 mm radius sphere.

span.quote: We opted to not use increasingly popular standardization approaches (for example, mean-regression, mean centering +/− variance normalization) in the calculation of derivative values, as the test-retest framework provides users a unique opportunity to consider the reliability of site-related differences.

span.label: AND THE PAPER DOES NOT DO WHAT ITS TITLE PROMISES, AND SAYS SO: `formal test-retest reliability or reproducibility analyses ARE BEYOND THE SCOPE OF THE PRESENT DATA DESCRIPTION`
span.term: AND THE PAPER DOES NOT DO WHAT ITS TITLE PROMISES, AND SAYS SO: `formal test-retest reliability or reproducibility analyses ARE BEYOND THE SCOPE OF THE PRESENT DATA DESCRIPTION`
span.quote: While formal test-retest reliability or reproducibility analyses are beyond the scope of the present data description, we illustrate the broad range of potential questions that can be answered for rfMRI, dMRI and sMRI using the resource.

span.label: `the SYNCHRONICITY of a voxel's time series and that of its NEAREST NEIGHBORS based on KENDALL'S COEFFICIENT OF CONCORDANCE to measure the local brain functional homogeneity`
span.quote: Regional Homogeneity (ReHo) 38–40 . The synchronicity of a voxel’s time series and that of its nearest neighbors based on Kendall’s coefficient of concordance to measure the local brain functional homogeneity.

span.label: `A MEASURE OF SUBJECT HEAD MOTION, which compares the motion between the current and previous volumes ... THE ROTATIONAL CHANGES ARE GIVEN DISTANCE VALUES BASED ON THE CHANGES ACROSS THE SURFACE OF A 50 MM RADIUS SPHERE`
span.quote: Mean framewise displacement (FD) 29 . A measure of subject head motion, which compares the motion between the current and previous volumes. This is calculated by summing the absolute value of displacement changes in the x, y and z directions and rotational changes about those three axes. The rotational changes are given distance values based on the changes across the surface of a 50 mm radius sphere.

span.label: 3-6 — the conventional span of a longitudinal developmental design, standing in for a minimum time nobody has defined
span.quote: Scan repeated at a distant time-point not believed to be developmentally equivalent. There is no exact definition of the minimum time for detecting developmental effects across scans, though designs typically span at least 3–6 months

span.label: 50 — the geometric convention converting head rotations into distances inside framewise displacement
span.quote: Mean framewise displacement (FD) 29 . A measure of subject head motion, which compares the motion between the current and previous volumes. This is calculated by summing the absolute value of displacement changes in the x, y and z directions and rotational changes about those three axes. The rotational changes are given distance values based on the changes across the surface of a 50 mm radius sphere.

span.label: 8 — the size of the posterior cingulate seed region that defines intrinsic functional connectivity here
span.quote: Intrinsic Functional Connectivity (iFC) of Posterior Cingulate Cortex (PCC) 41 . Using the mean time series from a spherical region of interest (diameter=8 mm) centered in PCC (x=−8, y=−56, z=26) 42 , functional connectivity with PCC is calculated for each voxel in the brain using Pearson’s correlation (results are Fisher r-to-z transformed).

span.label: the derivative whose between-site differences trace directly to the temporal sampling rate rather than to the brains measured
span.quote: In the case of fALFF, site-specific differences can be directly related to the temporal sampling rate (that is, TR; see Figure 3 ), as lower TR datasets include a broader range of frequencies in the denominator—thereby reducing the resulting fALFF scores (differences in aliasing are likely to be present as well). This note of caution about fALFF raises the general issue that rfMRI estimates can be highly sensitive to acquisition parameters
